{{Short description|Recursively-formed graph with two terminal vertices}}
[[Image:Series parallel composition.svg|thumb|upright=1.25|Series and parallel composition operations for series–parallel graphs]]

In [[graph theory]], '''series–parallel graphs''' are graphs with two distinguished vertices called ''terminals'', formed recursively by two simple composition operations. They can be used to model [[series and parallel circuits|series and parallel electric circuits]].

==Definition and terminology==
In this context, the term graph means [[multigraph]].

There are several ways to define series–parallel graphs. 

===First definition===
The following definition basically follows the one used by [[David Eppstein]].<ref name=eppstein>{{cite journal|author=Eppstein, David|author-link=David Eppstein|url=http://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/pubs/Epp-IC-92.pdf|title=Parallel recognition of series–parallel graphs|journal=[[Information and Computation]]|volume=98|issue=1|pages=41–55|year=1992|doi=10.1016/0890-5401(92)90041-D}}</ref>

A '''two-terminal graph''' ('''TTG''') is a graph with two distinguished vertices, {{mvar|s}} and {{mvar|t}}, called ''source'' and ''sink'', respectively.

The '''parallel composition''' {{math|1=''Pc'' = ''Pc''(''X'', ''Y'')}} of two TTGs {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} is a TTG created from the  [[disjoint union of graphs]] {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} by [[vertex merging|merging]] the sources of {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} to create the source of {{mvar|Pc}} and merging the sinks of {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} to create the sink of {{mvar|Pc}}.

The '''series composition''' {{math|1=''Sc'' = ''Sc''(''X'', ''Y'')}} of two TTGs {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} is a TTG created from the  disjoint union of graphs {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} by merging the sink of {{mvar|X}} with the source of {{mvar|Y}}. The source of {{mvar|X}} becomes the source of {{mvar|Sc}} and the sink of {{mvar|Y}} becomes the sink of {{mvar|Sc}}.

A '''two-terminal series–parallel graph''' ('''TTSPG''') is a graph that may be constructed by a sequence of  series and parallel compositions starting from a set of copies of a single-edge graph {{math|''[[complete graph|K]]''<sub>2</sub>}} with assigned terminals.

'''''Definition 1'''''. Finally, a graph is called '''series–parallel''' ('''SP'''), if it is a TTSPG when some two of its vertices are regarded as source and sink.

In a similar way one may define series–parallel [[digraph (mathematics)|digraph]]s, constructed from copies of single-arc graphs, with arcs directed from the source to the sink.

===Second definition===
The following definition specifies the same class of graphs.<ref name=Duffin>{{cite journal|author=Duffin, R. J.|title=Topology of Series–Parallel Networks|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|volume=10|year=1965|pages=303–313|doi=10.1016/0022-247X(65)90125-3|issue=2|doi-access=free}}</ref>

'''''Definition 2'''''. A graph is an SP-graph, if it may be turned into {{math|''[[complete graph|K]]''<sub>2</sub>}} by a sequence of the following operations:
* Replacement of a pair of parallel edges with a single edge that connects their common endpoints
* Replacement of a pair of edges incident to a vertex of degree 2 other than {{mvar|s}} or {{mvar|t}} with a single edge.

==Properties==
Every series–parallel graph has [[treewidth]] at most 2 and [[branchwidth]] at most 2.<ref name=Graphclasses>{{cite book | last1=Brandstädt | first1=Andreas | author1-link=Andreas Brandstädt | first2=Van Bang | last2=Le | last3=Spinrad | first3=Jeremy P. | title=Graph classes: a survey | zbl=0919.05001 | series=SIAM Monographs on Discrete Mathematics. and Applications | volume=3 | location=Philadelphia, PA | publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] | isbn=978-0-898714-32-6 | year=1999 | pages=[https://archive.org/details/graphclassessurv0000bran/page/172 172–174] | url=https://archive.org/details/graphclassessurv0000bran/page/172 }}</ref>  Indeed, a graph has treewidth at most 2 if and only if it has branchwidth at most 2, if and only if every [[biconnected component]] is a series–parallel graph.<ref>{{Cite journal
| last1 = Bodlaender | first1 = H.  | author-link = Hans L. Bodlaender
| title = A partial ''k''-arboretum of graphs with bounded treewidth 
| journal = [[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|Theoretical Computer Science]]
| volume = 209 
| issue = 1–2
| pages = 1–45 
| year = 1998 
| doi = 10.1016/S0304-3975(97)00228-4
| hdl = 1874/18312 | hdl-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal
 | last1 = Hall | first1 = Rhiannon
 | last2 = Oxley | first2 = James
 | last3 = Semple | first3 = Charles
 | last4 = Whittle | first4 = Geoff
 | doi = 10.1006/jctb.2002.2120
 | issue = 1
 | journal = [[Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B]]
 | pages = 148–171
 | title = On matroids of branch-width three
 | volume = 86
 | year = 2002| doi-access = free
 }}</ref> The [[maximal element|maximal]] series–parallel graphs, graphs to which no additional edges can be added without destroying their series–parallel structure, are exactly the [[k-tree|2-trees]].

2-connected series–parallel graphs are characterised by having no subgraph [[Homeomorphism (graph theory)|homeomorphic]] to {{math|''K''<sub>4</sub>}}.<ref name=Graphclasses/>

Series parallel graphs may also be characterized by their [[ear decomposition]]s.<ref name=eppstein/>

==Computational complexity==
SP-graphs may be recognized in linear time<ref name=VTL>{{cite journal|author1=Valdes, Jacobo |author2=Tarjan, Robert E. |author2-link=Robert Tarjan |author3=Lawler, Eugene L. |author3-link=Eugene Lawler |title=The recognition of series parallel digraphs|journal=[[SIAM Journal on Computing]]|volume=11|year=1982|pages=289–313|doi=10.1137/0211023|issue=2}}</ref> and their series–parallel decomposition may be constructed in linear time as well.

Besides being a model of certain types of electric networks, these graphs are of interest in [[computational complexity theory]], because a number of standard graph problems are solvable in linear time on SP-graphs,<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Takamizawa | first1 = K.
 | last2 = Nishizeki | first2 = T. | author2-link = Takao Nishizeki
 | last3 = Saito | first3 = N.
 | doi = 10.1145/322326.322328
 | issue = 3
 | journal = [[Journal of the ACM]]
 | pages = 623–641
 | title = Linear-time computability of combinatorial problems on series–parallel graphs
 | volume = 29
 | year = 1982| s2cid = 16082154
 | doi-access = free
 }}</ref> including finding of the [[maximum matching]], [[maximum independent set]], [[minimum dominating set]] and [[Hamiltonian completion]]. Some of these problems are [[NP-complete]] for general graphs. The solution capitalizes on the fact that if the answers for one of these problems are known for two SP-graphs, then one can quickly find the answer for their series and parallel compositions.

==Generalization==
The '''generalized series–parallel graphs''' ('''GSP-graphs''') are an extension of the SP-graphs<ref>{{cite journal|author=Korneyenko, N. M.|title=Combinatorial algorithms on a class of graphs|journal=[[Discrete Applied Mathematics]]|volume=54|issue=2–3|pages=215–217|year=1994|doi=10.1016/0166-218X(94)90022-1|doi-access=free}} Translated from ''Notices of the BSSR Academy of Sciences, Ser. Phys.-Math. Sci.'', (1984) no. 3, pp.&nbsp;109–111 {{in lang|ru}}</ref> with the same [[algorithmic efficiency]] for the mentioned problems. The class of GSP-graphs include the classes of SP-graphs and [[outerplanar graph]]s.

GSP graphs may be specified by ''Definition 2'' augmented with the third operation of [[vertex deletion|deletion]] of a dangling vertex (vertex of degree 1). Alternatively, ''Definition 1'' may be augmented with the following operation.

:The '''source merge''' {{math|1=''S'' = ''M''(''X'', ''Y'')}} of two TTGs {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} is a TTG created from the  disjoint union of graphs {{mvar|X}} and {{mvar|Y}} by merging the source of {{mvar|X}} with the source of {{mvar|Y}}. The source and sink of {{mvar|X}} become the source and sink of {{mvar|S}} respectively.

An [[SPQR tree]] is a tree structure that can be defined for an arbitrary [[vertex connectivity|2-vertex-connected graph]]. It has S-nodes, which are analogous to the series composition operations in series–parallel graphs, P-nodes, which are analogous to the parallel composition operations in series–parallel graphs, and R-nodes, which do not correspond to series–parallel composition operations. A 2-connected graph is series–parallel if and only if there are no R-nodes in its SPQR tree.
